fitness-tracker.title: FitTrack Fitness Tracker
fitness-tracker.description: A premium, mobile-first workout companion built for serious lifters. Not a step counter. Plan your training, execute sessions, track every set, and turn raw gym data into actionable insights.
fitness-tracker.problem: Generic fitness apps often focus on step counting or cardio, leaving serious lifters with clunky spreadsheets or basic notes. They lack specialized features like rep-aware warm-up generators, real-time rest timers that don't reset when switching apps, and instant access to PR history during a live session. Existing solutions often feel sluggish or require too many taps in a high-intensity gym environment.
fitness-tracker.solution: FitTrack was built as a performance-first PWA that prioritizes speed and data density. It features a specialized 'Live Session' mode with persistent timers, an intelligent PR detection engine that provides O(1) lookups for any exercise, and a server-rendered architecture that ensures sub-second load times even on weak gym Wi-Fi.

features.title: Three-Mode Workout Logging
features.description: Live Session with real-time rest timers, Manual History Log for past sessions, and Plan Designer for programming. Each mode has distinct behavior. Rest timer only fires in Live Session, warm-up sets never persist.

features.title: Intelligent PR Detection
features.description: Automated detection of Weight PRs and Rep PRs using a materialized ExerciseRecords collection. O(1) lookups on the gym floor. No scan, no lag. Atomic $max/$set updates preserve data integrity.

features.title: PR Timeline & 1RM Tracking
features.description: Per-exercise progress chart with max weight line, Epley estimated 1RM curve (server-side), and volume bars. Time-range selector: 1M / 3M / 6M / 1Y / Custom. Filtered client-side after a single fetch.

features.title: Warm-up Set Generator
features.description: Rep-aware scheme selection: STRENGTH (4 sets at 30-90%) down to ENDURANCE (1 set at 60%). Pure client-side calculation. Zero DB calls. Warm-up sets are never saved to WorkoutLog.

features.title: Plan vs Actual Adherence
features.description: Weekly schedule tracking with real adherence scores. Missed workouts are only flagged for past days. Future planned sessions stay open. Sessions matched to plans by date, not foreign key.

features.title: Shareable Workout Snapshots
features.description: Custom image generation via html2canvas creates Instagram-ready cards with PR badges, volume stats, and session highlights. Ready to share directly from the completion screen.

features.title: Consistency Heatmap
features.description: GitHub-style 52-week training frequency grid with sticky day labels and auto-scroll to current week. High visual impact. Turns habit data into a motivating, at-a-glance streak visualization.

features.title: Smart Rest Timer
features.description: Auto-starts after each completed set with useRef-based interval (never inside useState). Custom rest duration per exercise in Plan Designer. Haptic + audio alerts at countdown end.

upcomingIdeas.title: AI Session Debrief
upcomingIdeas.description: After completing a workout, the Anthropic API synthesizes WorkoutLog + ExerciseRecords to generate a post-session summary. PRs hit, volume compared to last session, and a focused recommendation for what to improve next time.

upcomingIdeas.title: AI Program Generator
upcomingIdeas.description: Input your goal (strength / hypertrophy / endurance), training days per week, and available equipment. The model generates a full multi-week periodized plan, directly saved to the Plans collection.

items.title: Materialized View Pattern
items.sub: ExerciseRecords acts as a denormalized cache for current PRs. Eliminates full WorkoutLog scans on every set completion.

items.title: MongoDB Aggregation Pipelines
items.sub: Complex $unwind → $group → $sort pipelines for analytics. Zero-weight sets filtered at the DB layer, never client-side.

items.title: Server-first Data Fetching
items.sub: All sidebar data fetched in page Server Components via Promise.all. No client-side useEffect waterfalls. Each fetch independently try/catch'd.

items.title: Glassmorphism Design System
items.sub: GlassCard primitive with consistent backdrop-filter, dark surface tokens, and orange-500 accent throughout. Mobile-first, one-hand usable between sets.

items.title: PWA + Service Workers
items.sub: Background rest timer notifications via Web Notifications API. Offline-resilient architecture planned for gym environments with no signal.

items.title: Custom useSessionStats Hook
items.sub: Unified live session state. Volume, sets, estimated time remaining, PR feed. Shared between sidebar and mobile variants via a single hook.

items.title: Epley 1RM (Server-only)
items.sub: weight × (1 + reps/30) always computed in a Server Action. Architecture rule enforced to avoid stale client-side estimates in charts.

items.title: Work-based Calorie Estimation
items.sub: Custom algorithm using total volume moved + sets completed. Accurate regardless of rest duration or timer fluctuations. Not a generic MET calculation.

portfolio-redesign.title: Conversational Developer Portfolio
portfolio-redesign.description: Command-driven personal portfolio built with Next.js App Router and Framer Motion. Replacing infinite scroll with a contextual AI chat interface that surfaces projects, skills, and experience on demand.
portfolio-redesign.problem: Traditional portfolios are often static, linear, and force recruiters to dig through buried links to find relevant info. They lack engagement and don't demonstrate a developer's ability to build truly interactive, product-like experiences. In a market flooded with 'infinite scroll' resumes, it's hard to stand out without a unique interaction model.
portfolio-redesign.solution: I designed a conversational UI that inverts the browsing experience. Instead of searching, visitors 'ask' for what they need via a command palette or chat interface. Built with Next.js App Router and Framer Motion, it provides sub-second transitions and a premium, tool-like feel that mirrors modern AI applications.
features: Command-palette-style interface with slash-command routing. Visitors type intent, not keywords
Framer Motion layout animations for seamless content transitions between project detail views
Server-rendered shell with client-side hydration. Fast initial load with no layout shift (zero CLS)
JSON-driven content architecture. All portfolio data decoupled from UI components for easy updates

upcomingIdeas.title: Live Claude API integration
upcomingIdeas.description: Replace simulated responses with real Claude API calls. Making the portfolio genuinely answer recruiter and client questions about specific projects, stack choices, and availability.

upcomingIdeas.title: RAG over resume & projects
upcomingIdeas.description: Embed resume, project write-ups, and GitHub READMEs into a pgvector store so the chat can retrieve and cite specific achievements in context.

upcomingIdeas.title: Visitor analytics dashboard
upcomingIdeas.description: Track which projects and questions visitors ask most. Feeding insights back into which work to feature or expand in the portfolio.

upcomingIdeas.title: Voice input via Web Speech API
upcomingIdeas.description: Let mobile visitors speak queries naturally. Further differentiating the experience from every static portfolio in the market.

content.text: Rethinking the portfolio as a product

Traditional portfolios force visitors to navigate a predetermined structure. This portfolio inverts that model. The visitor drives the conversation. Using Next.js App Router for SSR performance and Framer Motion for layout-aware transitions, the interface feels like a premium AI product rather than a developer resume.

hooked-on-movies.title: HookedOnMovies
hooked-on-movies.description: Full-stack media discovery platform built on Next.js with SSR/ISR, a TypeScript normalization layer across TMDB's Movie & TV APIs, and sub-second TTFB via parallel server-side data fetching.
hooked-on-movies.problem: Many movie discovery apps suffer from 'data fragmentation'. Fetching from multiple endpoints leads to inconsistent UI states and slow loading (waterfalls). Additionally, TMDB's API returns different schemas for Movies vs TV Shows, often causing runtime errors if not handled with rigorous type safety.
hooked-on-movies.solution: I implemented a custom TypeScript normalization layer that reconciles all TMDB entities into a single unified interface. To solve the performance issue, I architected a parallel fetching strategy using Promise.all on the server side, combined with ISR to keep trending content fresh without sacrificing speed.
features: TypeScript data normalization layer that reconciles inconsistent TMDB Movie vs TV Show field schemas into a single unified interface. Eliminating runtime type errors across the entire app
Parallel server-side data fetching with Promise.all across multiple TMDB endpoints, cutting TTFB significantly versus sequential waterfall requests
ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) on detail pages. Content stays fresh without per-request SSR cost, ideal for high-traffic title pages
Full SEO implementation: dynamic Open Graph tags, structured metadata per page, and canonical URLs for discoverability on search engines

upcomingIdeas.title: Personalized recommendation engine
upcomingIdeas.description: Replace TMDB's basic 'similar' endpoint with an embedding-based recommender (OpenAI embeddings + cosine similarity) that learns from a user's watch history and ratings.

upcomingIdeas.title: User accounts + persistent watchlists
upcomingIdeas.description: Add NextAuth.js with Google OAuth, PostgreSQL-backed watchlists, and per-user recommendation personalization that persists across sessions.

upcomingIdeas.title: Streaming availability via JustWatch API
upcomingIdeas.description: Show which platform (Netflix, Prime, Hotstar, etc.) each title is currently available on. Bridging discovery to instant action.

upcomingIdeas.title: Redis edge caching for TMDB responses
upcomingIdeas.description: Cache API responses at the CDN edge with configurable Redis TTLs to eliminate redundant TMDB calls and achieve sub-100ms global response times.

content.text: HookedOnMovies is a production-quality media discovery platform with a focus on performance, type safety, and cinematic UX. Users can explore trending content, view rich metadata, watch trailers, and surface recommendations. With a UI that competes visually with commercial streaming platforms.

TMDB's API returns fundamentally different shapes for movies versus TV shows. A custom TypeScript normalization layer maps both into a single shared interface consumed across all components. Eliminating defensive nullchecks throughout the codebase. Combined with Promise.all parallel fetching on the server, page data is assembled in a single round-trip rather than a waterfall.

Demonstrates end-to-end ownership of a full-stack Next.js product: API integration architecture, TypeScript system design, ISR caching strategy, SEO implementation, and a polished Framer Motion UI. All shipped as a cohesive, performant application.
